ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against: (i) French PEP list maintained by Tracfin (Unité de traitement de l'information financière); (ii) EU Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iv) OFAC SDN and Non-SDN Lists; (v) French asset freeze register (Registre national des gels) under Art. L.562-1 CMF; (vi) World Bank Debarrment List; (vii) INTERPOL Red Notices. Screening must be refreshed at least annually and upon each material change. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) mandatory for any UBO residing in FATF blacklist/greyslist jurisdictions. Tracfin Declaration de Soupcon required within 48 hours of suspicious activity detection under Art. L.561-15 CMF.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-32 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Articles L.210-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); Decree No. 2023-179 of 6 March 2023 establishing the INPI Guichet Unique for business formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) – Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with automatic transmission to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) and to INSEE for SIREN/SIRET assignment.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de Création d'une Personne Morale (Form M0), filed exclusively through the INPI Guichet Unique; legal existence is evidenced by the Extrait Kbis issued by the RCS greffe.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SAS has no statutory minimum capital (Article L.227-2, Code de commerce); the Articles freely fix the capital (in practice €1 or more). At least 50% of the nominal value of each cash subscription must be released at incorporation, with the balance payable within 5 years; in-kind contributions must be fully released at formation. Cash funds must be deposited and blocked in a dedicated French bank account or with a notary (attestation de dépôt des fonds) until the RCS delivers the Kbis. 100% non-resident ownership is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDER SHAREHOLDER OF [SAS NAME] — The founder shareholder, acting under Articles L.227-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code, hereby resolves: (1) the share capital fixed in the Articles of Association is fully subscribed and allotted; the corresponding cash contribution has been deposited in the Company's escrow account; (2) the registered office is adopted as set forth in the Articles, and the President is authorized to execute the occupancy agreement; (3) [NAME] is appointed Président of the SAS with full powers to bind the Company, open bank accounts and represent it toward third parties; (4) the President is authorized to publish the legal notice, file the incorporation dossier with the INPI Guichet Unique, and cure any procedural queries. Effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Signing and Subscription of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founder shareholders (private act, acte sous seing privé) or Notaire (optional); no public administration involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French stipulating the SAS corporate form, corporate purpose (software programming, APE code 6201Z, mobile utility applications), corporate name, registered office, duration (99 years), share capital and cash contribution breakdown, share transfer restrictions, and the first President. Each founder signs the Statuts; the President accepts office in a separate annex. Non-EU founders must provide passport and proof of address.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts
Share subscription list (état des souscriptions et versements)
Acceptance letter of the President (acte de nomination du Président)
Passport/ID of each shareholder and of the President
Proof of residential address of shareholders
Beneficial owner information (incorporated in the M0)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe queries the Statuts, amend them by a shareholder decision (acte modificatif) and resubmit within the 15-day regularization period; if refused, petition the Juge du registre (President of the Tribunal de Commerce).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Deposit of the Share Capital and Delivery of the Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank, online bank, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a Notaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder opens a provisional blocked account in the future corporate name and deposits the cash portion of the capital. The bank or notary issues an attestation de dépôt des fonds certifying the amount and blocking of the funds until the Kbis is delivered; the funds are unblocked only upon presentation of the Kbis.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
KYC package: corporate documentation of founders, beneficial-owner declaration, passport copies
Proof of French business address (lease or domiciliation contract)
Wire reference or deposit receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account, deposit the capital with a Notaire instead, or invoke the right-to-bank procedure (droit au compte, Article L.312-1 of the Code monétaire et financier) through the Banque de France.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Notice of Incorporation in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legally authorized legal-announcement newspaper (JAL) of the département of the registered office, through accredited publishers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and pay for the legal announcement (avis de constitution) containing the corporate name, form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, RCS city, and identity of the President. The publisher delivers an attestation de parution with the announcement number, which must be attached to the registration file before filing the M0.
required_dossiers: Company details (name, legal form, capital, registered office)
Corporate purpose text as set out in the Statuts
Identity of the first President
Order form and proof of payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication proof is rejected for incomplete content, publish a corrective notice (rectificatif) and resubmit the original attestation within the regularization window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the M0 Declaration through the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); data transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) and INSEE (Sirene)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a professional account, select 'Création de société', complete the M0 declaration with company identity, registered office and justification of occupancy (lease, domiciliation contract), beneficial-owner declaration, and President appointment. Upload all required dossiers in PDF, pay the registry fee electronically, and submit. The file is routed to the RCS greffe of the competent commercial court, which issues the Extrait Kbis within the legal deadline of 5 business days after the file is complete.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts (PDF, certified copy)
Attestation de dépôt des fonds (capital escrow certificate)
Attestation de parution of the legal announcement
Justification of registered office (lease or occupancy letter)
Identity document of the President and power of attorney if filed by an agent
Declaration of beneficial owners
Company RIB (bank details) for tax purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For a notice of incompleteness, the applicant has 15 days to complete the file electronically; for a refusal, submit a new complete declaration and, if the greffe exceeds the legal deadline, apply to the judge supervising the registry (Juge chargé du contrôle du registre, Tribunal de Commerce).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Token Issuance and Operational Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS), INSEE (Sirene), Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), and the chosen commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, collect the Extrait Kbis, SIREN/SIRET numbers, and APE code 6201Z. Present the Kbis to the bank to convert the provisional capital account into the definitive corporate account and unblock escrowed funds. Register the company with URSSAF (social security) and verify the EU VAT number obtained via the DGFiP. For the mobile utility app, open the Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console developer accounts under the registered entity.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis
SIREN/SIRET confirmation notice
Corporate bank account contract
Attestation de dépôt de fonds (for unblocking)
App store listing and developer program documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGFiP delays the VAT number, request an attestation of VAT status via the impots.gouv.fr professional account; if INSEE assigns an incorrect APE code, file a rectification declaration through the Guichet Unique with supporting documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial establishment. General business and labor supervision: Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating permit required for ISIC 6201 (software programming and mobile application publishing) under French law; the activity is subject only to RCS registration evidenced by the Kbis.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique / DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based software activity, not listed in the ICPE nomenclature (Annexe to Article R.511-9 of the Code de l'environnement); no full EIA or environmental registration required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges or VOC emissions generated. Compliance limited to: EU WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU and Articles L.541-21-2 et seq. of the Code de l'environnement for e-waste from IT equipment; general office waste sorting obligations; no wastewater discharge permit needed for standard office use.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For leased office premises: verify the landlord's fire safety compliance certificate and ERP classification (category 5 if applicable), electrical installation conformity certificate, and compliance with workplace health-and-safety rules under Articles L.4111-1 et seq. of the Code du travail; for remote-first app development, no physical operational clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finances (Direction générale des finances publiques, DGFiP), administered through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official impots.gouv.fr portal. Business formation and registration data are submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS obtains its statutory identifiers through the INPI Guichet unique registration filing. The filing generates a SIREN number for the legal entity, a SIRET number for each establishment, and an activity code. The entity applies for corporate income tax and VAT accounts with the competent SIE, generally using the initial tax registration information and the VAT registration request. The French VAT identification number is issued by the DGFiP and normally has the format FR followed by a two-character check key and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity with a French fixed establishment registers through the relevant SIE after obtaining the applicable French establishment identifiers. A non-established foreign taxable person making taxable French supplies must generally register with the Non-Resident Tax Service (Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères) unless the transaction is subject to domestic reverse charge or is reported through an applicable EU One Stop Shop scheme. EU-established businesses may use the Union OSS for qualifying cross-border B2C digital services; OSS does not replace domestic registration for supplies outside its scope.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) by default. An eligible SAS may elect temporarily for income tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, IR) if statutory conditions are satisfied, including qualifying ownership, size, age, activity, and non-listed status requirements; the election is time-limited and must be notified within the statutory period. There is no general US-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules apply to arrangements producing deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes; they operate as statutory restrictions and do not constitute an elective entity-classification regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT), based on the EU VAT Directive and French Tax Code. Cross-border digital services are governed by place-of-supply, customer-status, and OSS rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a France-established business eligible for the domestic VAT franchise for services, the ordinary prior-year turnover threshold is generally EUR 37,500 and the current-year tolerance threshold is generally EUR 41,250, subject to statutory category rules and legislative change. For sales of goods, the ordinary and tolerance thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 and EUR 93,500. These thresholds do not provide a general exemption for non-established suppliers making taxable French supplies. A supplier established in one EU Member State may generally apply the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold for qualifying intra-EU B2C telecommunications, broadcasting, and electronically supplied services, after which destination-country VAT applies; the supplier may elect to apply destination-country taxation from the outset and use OSS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing for domestic B2B transactions between French-established taxable persons and mandatory electronic transaction reporting for specified cross-border B2B and B2C transactions. The current statutory timetable provides mandatory receipt capability for all businesses from 1 September 2026, mandatory issuance for large and medium-sized businesses from 1 September 2026, and mandatory issuance for small and micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027, subject to any legislative amendments or approved extensions. Invoices will generally be exchanged through an approved private electronic invoicing platform (plateforme agréée) or the public platform framework designated by law; structured data and required transaction fields must be transmitted to the DGFiP. France does not currently operate a universal real-time invoice-clearance requirement for ordinary domestic invoices. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. Electronic invoicing does not generally replace OSS reporting for qualifying cross-border B2C digital services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the EU may be VAT-exempt with the right to deduct input VAT where the supplier proves that the goods left the EU customs territory and satisfies invoicing, accounting, and customs requirements. The exemption is supported by customs exit records, including the electronic export declaration and exit results. Intra-EU supplies of goods may qualify for the separate intra-Community exemption when the customer has a valid VAT number in another Member State, the goods are dispatched or transported to that Member State, and the supplier retains required evidence and reporting. Services supplied to a business customer are generally taxed at the customer's location under the B2B place-of-supply rule and may be reported without French VAT under reverse charge; this is generally a place-of-supply outcome rather than a French zero-rated export. Electronically supplied B2C services are taxed in the customer's Member State under destination-based rules, with OSS available where applicable. Input VAT refunds require valid purchase invoices, a direct business connection, proper accounting, and timely VAT return or refund-claim support.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration and customs export movement reference
Electronic confirmation that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, and VAT treatment
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, or carrier delivery record
Packing list and, where applicable, export licence or other regulatory authorization
Proof of payment or commercial settlement where relevant to the audit file
For intra-EU supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number, transport evidence, and required EC Sales List reporting
For digital services, customer-location evidence, billing records, IP or payment data where relevant, and OSS records if the Union OSS is used
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline of 180 days for export VAT relief. Export evidence must nevertheless be retained and produced to establish that goods actually left the EU and that the VAT exemption conditions were met. If the exemption or deduction is unsupported, the DGFiP may assess the unpaid VAT, deny or claw back input VAT, charge late-payment interest, and impose penalties. The penalty may generally be 10% for certain late or incomplete compliance failures, 40% for deliberate failure or deliberate inaccuracy, and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres, abuse of law, or concealed activity, subject to the applicable facts and statutory provisions. False customs declarations may trigger customs penalties and, in serious cases, criminal proceedings. Statutory limitation periods commonly allow reassessment within three years for VAT, subject to extended periods for fraud, concealed activity, or criminal conduct. A prudent audit file should preserve customs exit evidence, invoices, transport records, customer-status evidence, digital-service location evidence, VAT returns, OSS returns, and payment records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) — Direction Générale des Relations Financières avec l'Étranger, operating within the Eurosystem/ESCB framework and coordinating with the European Central Bank and the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) on external financial relations and direct investment screening under Articles L151-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the euro framework (Article 63 TFEU; Directive 88/361/EEC; Articles L151-1 to L165-2 CMF). No prior exchange-control authorization is required for profit repatriation, dividend distributions, or loan repayments by a French SAS to non-resident shareholders; however, dividend and interest outflows may trigger withholding tax (30% default under Article 119 bis CGI, reduced to 5–15% or 0% under applicable DTT and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive) and are reportable on the Banque de France balance-of-payments (BOP) statistical declaration. Foreign direct investment in 'strategic sectors' (Article R151-3 CMF), including dual-use or critical-infrastructure data activities, requires prior approval from the Ministry of Economy; a mobile utility app (ISIC 6201) with no critical-infrastructure nexus does NOT trigger this control. Bank financing from non-EU lenders is subject to arm's-length substance requirements under Article 155-A CGI to prevent recharacterization of interest as deemed dividends, and to automatic BOP reporting thresholds (€15 million direct investment).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export proceeds or App Store/Google Play settlement revenues. Receipts may be held in EUR or any freely-convertible foreign currency in resident or non-resident accounts; the only ongoing obligation is statistical declaration to the Banque de France via the bank's automated BOP monitoring system (monthly reporting of cross-border payments, with direct investment transactions requiring a dedicated declaration when exceeding €15 million per calendar year).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte de Dépôt Professionnel) + Blocked Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué) for SAS incorporation
Operational Account (Compte Courant Professionnel) + Multi-currency Sub-account (Compte Devises) for USD/GBP settlements
Operational Account + FX Hedge Collateral Account
Operational Account (digital-native onboarding; fintech partner ecosystem)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for day-to-day treasury operations using EU-licensed EMIs and fintech banks (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Revolut Business Luxembourg, Airwallex via EU passporting), which offer remote onboarding, multi-currency IBANs, and SWIFT/SEPA API rails; however, such EMIs have LOW viability for the mandatory blocked capital escrow account required during SAS incorporation, because the French Commercial Code (Article L227-2 CGI-compliant deposit rules) requires funds to be deposited with a credit institution or a notary (Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations) capable of issuing a legal attestation de dépôt des fonds. Offshore non-EU EMIs (e.g., Singapore/HK-based) have LOW viability as primary settlement banks because Apple and Google payout contracts typically require a Eurozone IBAN, and Banque de France AML expectations favor licensed French/EU institutions for the €10,000+ receipt threshold.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch attendance is not legally mandated; all tier-1 French banks permit remote onboarding via certified video-identification procedures conforming to Article R561-17 CMF (ACP/AMF guidance), provided the Président and each UBO holding ≥25% submits notarized passports, proof of residential address (<3 months), and a corporate KYC pack. In practice, an in-person or video interview is universally required for the President (mandataire) before account activation; non-EU resident UBOs or complex offshore holding structures may trigger a compliance-committee escalation requiring a physical visit to a branch or a French notary. The SAS must also file the IN-UBO form with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, which the bank will verify against the registration extract (Kbis).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital-only business model with no physical storefront; free-to-download app monetized via Apple/Google in-app purchases raising anonymous counterparty risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement; 12 months of Apple/Google settlement reports; app privacy policy and consent architecture; audited technical architecture demonstrating no crypto, gambling, or high-risk payment functionality; 3-year business plan with user-acquisition metrics (DAU/MAU, installs).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or multi-jurisdictional UBO chain with potential offshore intermediate holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully certified IN-UBO declaration; share register extract and nominal-value share subscription list; corporate organization chart from ultimate natural persons to the SAS; notarized passport copies of all UBOs (≥25%); proof of residential address (<3 months); source-of-funds documentation for the capital injection (shareholder bank statements, share-purchase agreements).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SAS expecting immediate high-volume, low-value IAP receivables with disproportionate revenue-to-history ratio
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with 3-year revenue forecast; app store listing analytics (installs, conversion rates); payout contracts with Apple (iTunes Sàrl, Luxembourg) and Google (Google Ireland Ltd); initial bank statements of the contracting entities; French tax clearance status (avis de situation) or prior-period accounts (liasse fiscale) if available; commitment to monthly settlement reconciliations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential money-laundering via refund/chargeback manipulation between app stores and the SAS treasury
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented refund policy and chargeback handling procedure; Apple/Google monthly refund reports cross-referenced to settlement statements; internal accounting control framework (segregation of duties); statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) engagement letter once the SAS exceeds audit thresholds; independent reconciliation certificate if requested by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cumulative cross-border transactions exceeding €10,000 without demonstrable commercial substance (trade-settlement red flag under 4AMLD/5AMLD enhanced due diligence)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements with cloud infrastructure providers (AWS/GCP/Azure), subcontractors, and licensing counterparties; detailed invoice trail with PO reconciliation; IBAN consistency checks; annual BOP statistical declarations filed through the bank; FATCA/CRS self-certifications for any foreign account holders or payees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001.001.03) for EU/EEA shareholders, or (ii) SWIFT MT103 (field 70 remittance info, field 72 bank-to-bank) for non-EEA shareholders, with ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (Equity) or 'CAPC' (Capital Contribution) and French BOP narrative 'Apport en capital social – prise de participation directe'. Funds must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) at a licensed credit institution or retained by a notary until (a) the articles of association (statuts) are signed and (b) the SAS obtains its Kbis extract upon registration with the RCS (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce); release requires presentation of the Kbis and the attestation de dépôt des fonds. Supporting verification bundle: executed statuts; shareholder subscription list with share counts and nominal value (typically €1/share); shareholder board resolution approving the capital increase; IN-UBO declaration; bank source-of-funds form.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (XML pain.001.001.03) for EUR-denominated EU payables — cloud hosting, SaaS licensing, French subcontractors, payroll via B2B payroll providers; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA/non-EUR disbursements — North America/APAC contractors, trademark filings, insurance premiums, with field 70 containing contract and invoice references; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) are legally permissible but commercially nonstandard for software licensing transactions — recommended only for hardware procurement or a distribution agreement requiring documentary evidence; (iv) Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlements are received in EUR via SEPA from Apple (iTunes Sàrl, Luxembourg) and Google (Google Ireland Ltd), eliminating the need for manual FX conversion on the receivable side. All outbound payments above €10,000 equivalent require updated counterparty KYC files; FATCA/CRS declarations are maintained automatically by the paying bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain Vanilla Outright Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) with tenors up to 24 months, entered with licensed credit institutions under ISDA 2002 or French FBF master agreements
FX Swaps (spot-starting with forward leg ≤ 12 months) for temporary liquidity rebalancing between EUR and USD accounts
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for non-EUR term debt or lease liabilities, subject to EMIR clearing and margin obligations
Zero-Cost Collars and Vanilla FX Options (both purchased and sold components) to hedge projected Apple/Google settlement inflows in hard-currency pairs

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are permitted only against restricted or inconvertible counter-currencies (e.g., INR, CNY) for supplier-side exposure; they are NOT market-standard for EUR/USD or EUR/GBP because full convertibility eliminates the need, and any NDF is subject to EMIR reporting, clearing thresholds, and Banque de France BOP classification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary shareholders' meeting approving annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: N/A – internal corporate record retained in the company's minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year, unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct administrative penalty; however, absence of approved accounts prevents the timely deposit of annual financial statements and exposes the company to judicial summons and procedural fines at the request of any interested party.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the end of the fiscal year, following approval by the shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a judicial injunction, a periodic penalty payment (astreinte), and administrative fines; persistent non-compliance can lead to removal from the commercial and companies register (radiation).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal year, no later than 15 May of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within three months of fiscal year-end; electronic filing is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of assessed tax plus monthly late interest of 0.2%; after formal notice, repeated failure may raise the penalty to 10% of the tax due.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) – update on share transfer or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), filed via the electronic portal (INPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after any change in beneficial ownership; no recurring annual deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the DBE within the 15-day window exposes the legal entity to an administrative fine of up to EUR 7,500 under the Code monétaire et financier.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for an SAS if the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total assets exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (exclusive of tax) exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Appointment also becomes mandatory if required by the articles of association, or if the company forms part of a group requiring consolidation or controlled/corporate-structure audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (ANC Regulation 2016-07) as codified in the Code de commerce, applied to individual annual accounts; IFRS is permitted solely for consolidated statutory accounts of listed and certain public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation formality. The register of beneficial owners is kept current by filing an updated Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (DBE) with the RCS within 15 days of any change in beneficial ownership. Each share transfer must also be recorded in the registre des mouvements de titres, and the RCS cross-checks the shareholder record against the DBE on a periodic basis. Failure to keep the DBE aligned with share movements may result in administrative fines.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres (share transfer register)
Registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées et de décisions (minute book)
Registre du personnel (employee register, if employees are engaged)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – 600 annually for registered office / corporate secretarial agent services in major French cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,300 – 16,500 (EUR 3,000 – 15,000) for a full statutory audit; not required if the company remains below the statutory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax on taxable profits. Qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises may benefit from a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profits, subject to ownership, turnover and paid-up-capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: France provides a 15% SME rate on qualifying profits up to EUR 42,500; a research tax credit generally equal to 30% of eligible research expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold; a 20% innovation tax credit for qualifying SME innovation expenditure, subject to statutory limits; and an intellectual-property regime generally taxing qualifying net income from eligible IP at a separate 10% rate. Tax holidays may apply in specifically designated areas or regimes and require case-specific eligibility verification. Dividends received by a French parent from qualifying subsidiaries may receive a 95% exemption, subject to participation-exemption conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal at impots.gouv.fr using EFI or an accredited EDI provider. Form 2065 is accompanied by the relevant annual tax packages, principally Forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, and accounting schedules in the 2050-SD series.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly corporate income tax installments generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions. A final balance payment is generally due on the 15th day of the fourth month following the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, the annual return is generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is generally the second business day following 1 May of the following year. The tax administration may prescribe different dates for particular filing methods or periods.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS legal name, SIREN number, registered address, tax office, fiscal year opening and closing dates, activity code, turnover, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the French permanent establishment or subsidiary status. A French-resident SAS files on its worldwide taxable profit, subject to applicable treaty allocation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065, taxable profit or tax loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable profit or loss calculated from the commercial accounts after tax adjustments and transfer to the detailed 2058 schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude income not attributable to the French entity or French permanent establishment under the applicable tax treaty, while retaining contemporaneous attribution support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report corporate income tax due after applying the applicable 25% rate, qualifying SME rate, credits, installments and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not treat foreign taxes as automatically creditable; apply the relevant treaty or French statutory credit mechanism and maintain evidence of foreign payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to taxable profit through permanent and temporary additions and deductions, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation differences and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document all cross-border adjustments, permanent-establishment allocations, foreign exchange items and treaty-exempt income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report current-year losses, carried-forward losses, losses carried back where elected, and the amount of losses used against current taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French loss-utilization cap: generally EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Maintain loss-origin and expiry records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax credits, distribution information and other items required for the tax computation and shareholder disclosure framework.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile distributions to board approvals, shareholder registers, withholding tax returns and treaty-relief documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2059-E-SD, value added and intellectual-property information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report value-added, production, intellectual-property and other business indicators relevant to the tax package and applicable preferential regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the legal and economic owner of software, source code, trademarks and other IP; distinguish internally developed IP from acquired or licensed rights.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2059-F-SD and Form 2059-G-SD, shareholding and subsidiaries
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report qualifying participations, subsidiaries, ownership percentages and relevant group information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include non-French subsidiaries and document participation exemptions, dividend withholding tax, beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose tax withheld on payments to non-residents where applicable, including dividends, royalties, services or other French-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the applicable withholding return and obtain treaty-relief evidence before applying a reduced rate or exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Where applicable, summarize related-party transactions, transfer-pricing methodology, documentation status and the identity of related entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the form where statutory thresholds or group conditions are met and reconcile all amounts to the general ledger and Local File.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% after formal notice and potentially 80% in cases of fraudulent or abusive conduct. Late payment generally bears late-payment interest of 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Understatements may trigger interest, tax-geared penalties, denial of deductions or credits, and enhanced penalties for deliberate, abusive or fraudulent conduct. Failure to provide transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions lacking adequate documentation, subject to statutory limitations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD and electronic corporate tax package through impots.gouv.fr or an accredited EDI-TDFC provider
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The same annual filing deadline applies to the corporate tax package. Amendments should be filed promptly after identifying an error, with any additional tax and applicable interest paid without delay.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the normal corporate income tax regime, tax consolidation status, parent-company regime, and any special regime elected by the SAS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not make the SAS a non-resident taxpayer. The French SAS remains subject to French corporate tax on its own taxable results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile statutory accounts, tax accounts and supporting ledgers, including deductible expenses, depreciation, provisions, impairment, financing costs and employee-related expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply arm's-length pricing to all transactions with non-French related parties and retain agreements, invoices, allocation keys and benefit evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible tax credits only for documented qualifying expenditure and identify subcontractors, personnel, technical work and allocation calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign subcontracting and foreign personnel costs require specific eligibility analysis and documentary support; do not duplicate incentives claimed in another jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to substantiate tax credits can result in repayment, interest and penalties. Incorrect tax packages may be treated as inaccurate declarations even where the statutory return was filed on time.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic French withholding tax rate on dividends and similar distributions paid to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to exemptions and reduced treaty rates. A qualifying EU parent may obtain exemption under the French implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring a qualifying participation, minimum holding period and anti-abuse compliance. French resident individuals are generally subject to a 12.8% income tax withholding component, separate from social levies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test requirements, holding period and anti-abuse conditions, and apply the relevant treaty article. Where French administrative procedure requires prior authorization or a prescribed form, submit it to the competent French tax office before payment. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund or credit claim using the treaty, residence certificate, payment evidence, shareholder register, dividend resolution and proof of beneficial ownership. Reassess treaty entitlement for each payment and retain records for the statutory audit period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar IP payments to non-residents are generally subject to domestic withholding at 25%, with possible exemptions or reduced rates under an applicable treaty or the EU Interest and Royalties Directive. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions apply, including payments to entities in non-cooperative jurisdictions or payments recharacterized under specific anti-abuse rules. Treaty rates vary and must be confirmed under the applicable bilateral treaty. Related-party interest remains subject to French deductibility limitations, thin-capitalization rules, arm's-length pricing and anti-hybrid rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million turnover or gross assets, or specified group, ownership or related-party conditions connected with an entity meeting that threshold, generally trigger the full French Master File and Local File documentation framework under Articles L13 AA and L13 AB of the French Tax Procedures Code. An annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies at a lower EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold or where specified related-party or group conditions are met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a single standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore regimes. Substance is enforced through the arm's-length principle, beneficial-ownership requirements, the general anti-abuse rule, the principal-purpose test, controlled-foreign-company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation provisions and permanent-establishment doctrine. A French SAS should maintain real decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational control, premises or operational infrastructure, appropriate capitalization, functional risk control, IP governance and contemporaneous business purpose. An app business should specifically document product development, software ownership, user acquisition, platform agreements, payment flows, customer support and allocation of Apple and Google platform fees.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.transfer_pricing_operational_requirement: Intercompany arrangements must be written, commercially coherent and consistent with actual conduct. Benchmarking should cover software development, platform services, marketing, user support, data processing, cloud infrastructure, intra-group financing, IP licensing and management services. The French entity should preserve invoices, contracts, time records, cost-center data, allocation keys, benefit analyses, tested-party selection and year-end true-up calculations. The French tax administration may impose an arm's-length adjustment, deny unsupported deductions, recharacterize payments as distributions or apply withholding tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax filings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, manipulating App Store or Google Play receipts, fabricating expenses, using false invoices, omitting foreign accounts or deliberately understating taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment, late-payment interest, a 40% penalty for deliberate conduct and an 80% penalty for fraudulent conduct or certain abusive arrangements. Criminal tax fraud may carry imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000; aggravated cases may carry up to 7 years and EUR 3 million, with higher statutory limits in specified circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or de facto managers may incur civil tax liability under Article L267 of the French Tax Procedures Code where serious and repeated misconduct makes collection impossible. Criminal liability may include imprisonment, fines, confiscation, management bans and professional disqualification. A travel ban is not automatic but may be ordered by a court or investigative authority where legally justified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Overpriced related-party services, underpriced IP licenses, unsupported management charges, non-arm's-length loans, circular cash movements or year-end entries lacking commercial evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable-income adjustment, denial of deductions, withholding tax on recharacterized distributions, late-payment interest, 40% or 80% penalties depending on conduct, and transfer-pricing documentation penalties where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for breach of management duties, tax recovery proceedings in cases of serious and repeated misconduct, and criminal exposure if the arrangements form part of intentional tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, fictitious substance and permanent-establishment concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French SAS with nominal directors, no genuine business activity, no control over software or customer relationships, artificial invoicing, or shifting functions and risks abroad while French personnel conduct the business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the entity or arrangements, denial of treaty benefits, French permanent-establishment assessment, corporate tax reassessment, withholding tax, VAT consequences, interest and aggravated anti-abuse penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil and criminal liability for fraudulent use of the company, fictitious accounting or tax evasion. Courts may order management bans, asset confiscation and imprisonment where the underlying conduct constitutes an offence. A shell company is not independently unlawful if it is dormant and accurately disclosed, but false substance representations are high-risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Obscuring the ultimate beneficial owner, accepting unexplained third-party payments, routing funds through opaque entities, falsifying the register of beneficial owners, or failing to report suspicious activity where a regulated intermediary has a reporting duty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corrective orders, administrative fines, criminal penalties for laundering or related offences, confiscation of proceeds and enhanced penalties where organized crime or aggravated circumstances apply. Beneficial-owner registration failures may result in formal notices, fines and restrictions on corporate filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally prosecuted for knowing participation, concealment or facilitation. Sanctions can include imprisonment, fines, confiscation and management disqualification. Travel restrictions may be imposed only through applicable judicial or investigative procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying consumer app sales, failing to account for EU B2C digital-services VAT, incorrectly treating Apple or Google as the economic seller, omitting OSS filings, or claiming unsupported input VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment, interest, fixed or percentage-based penalties, denial of input VAT, joint-liability exposure in specified fraud situations and possible criminal sanctions for deliberate VAT fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability can arise for intentional fraud, serious management misconduct or obstruction of tax collection. Directors may also face criminal prosecution where VAT evasion is deliberate and material.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate distributions and unlawful profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends without distributable profits, disguising shareholder withdrawals as loans or expenses, omitting dividend withholding tax, or remitting royalties and interest without treaty entitlement or beneficial-owner evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restatement as unlawful distribution or hidden distribution, repayment claims, withholding tax assessment, interest, penalties, possible breach of French corporate-law rules and, in serious cases, misuse-of-corporate-assets or bankruptcy-related offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore improperly distributed assets and may be personally liable for management misconduct. Intentional misuse of company assets can result in imprisonment, fines, management bans and disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining incomplete books, deleting source-code or platform records, refusing electronic accounting files, falsifying ledgers, obstructing a tax audit or failing to preserve contracts and payment reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of accounts, assessment based on external evidence, non-cooperation penalties, tax reassessment, interest, aggravated penalties and criminal sanctions for forgery, obstruction or fraudulent accounting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted for falsification, obstruction or deliberate destruction of evidence and may face fines, imprisonment, confiscation and management disqualification.
